correctness.rationale: The four mutually orthogonal spectral projectors for K_{m,n} reconstruct all matrix entries of exp(-tL^2). Diagonal and cross-part entries are positive, leaving exactly two possible signed off-diagonal types. Row absolute sums yield an equality-attained exact norm. Differentiation proves one unique positive peak/root per negative-mass function. The explicit inequality at n>=32m separates the candidate peak heights; the signs at 2/n^2 order their recovery roots. Bracketing F_B(c/(mn))/m -> 1-c proves the asymptotic recovery horizon for arbitrary m>=2 with n/m->infinity; exact peak formulas give the remaining limits. Verify script independently tests small matrices and root/order calculations; it is not used to justify infinite cases.

value.rationale: Eventual positivity can coexist with transient endpoint amplification for fourth-order diffusion. The complete bipartite family has an independently motivated imbalance parameter and four eigenvalues, allowing a natural quantitative stability test. A sharp maximum-norm peak, an exact positivity threshold and their divergent asymptotic time ratio show a genuinely nontrivial distinction: norm amplification vanishes while the last negative entries persist much longer. The result applies to infinitely many graphs and gives exact extremizing sign input, not an isolated small numerical case or a tautological restatement of general semigroup convergence.
